Chapter Details: Status of national population, civil, address, land, business, electoral, tax and social protection registers. 44 variables in 8 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Does the government maintain a digital population register?
Comments: NCRA established 2016 for civil reg, digital system with ICT infra, multipurpose ID issuance, vital stats reports published.
revision_notes: Fetched both cited URLs: ncra.gov.sl/about (still live; confirms 2016 Act and NCRA's mandate to register all civil status events and issue a multi-purpose ID) and ncra.gov.sl/vital-statistics (still live; hosts 2022/2023 annual vital statistics reports). Neither source, on its own, evidences the register's deployment extent, so the cited basis for a score of 4 was thin. Ran a fresh search for current coverage data. Found NCRA's own reporting via Biometric Update (June 2025, quoting NCRA's Director of ICT at ID4Africa 2025) stating 93% national ID/civil registration coverage and over 80% of services digitised nationwide, plus a national identification number (NIN) issued to nearly all citizens and eligible non-citizens and used as the basis for identity verification across government services. This is corroborated by NCRA's own ID4Africa 2024 conference presentation showing registration coverage rising to over 90% by 2022-2024 on a fully digital, centrally maintained eCRVS/ID platform. Together these are authoritative, current (2024-2025), and consistent, supporting a recalculation to the top of the scale (5 = Fully deployed nationwide). As this is a top-of-scale promotion it is flagged for human review per protocol rather than being merged automatically.
revised_comments: The National Civil Registration Authority (NCRA), established under the National Civil Registration Act 2016, operates an integrated Civil Registration, Vital Statistics and Identity Management System that functions as Sierra Leone's national population register. As of mid-2025 the NCRA reports 93% national ID and civil registration coverage of the eligible population, with over 80% of its services digitised and a unique National Identification Number (NIN) issued to citizens and eligible non-citizens. The register is centrally maintained, biometrically verified, and used as the basis for identity verification across government services nationwide.
